chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:
I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'There are dirhams due to me from a man, and he says to me,

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem/It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell an item to a debtor at a higher price in exchange for delaying payment of a debt?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) validates a specific debt-deferral mechanism where a creditor sells an item to the debtor at an inflated price to delay repayment, ruling it permissible (*la ba'sa bihi*). This highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between this commercial arrangement and *riba al-jahiliyya*, as the profit is derived from the sale price rather than a fixed interest on the debt itself, provided the transaction is genuine and not merely a disguise for usury.
